input.rationale: Bound the removed-leader ReadIndex finding with a control for the same cause: the harness now also runs the identical removal in a three-voter cluster, where the reduced configuration has two voters and the singleton shortcut cannot apply. The comparison set retains the single-voter scenario and adds the control's observations, so a future receipt can distinguish the stale immediate answer from the alternative explanation that the removed leader merely keeps operating as a leader for reads. No interpretation is added this turn; the question's account stays as recorded until the receipt exists.

scope.description: Observe the removed-leader ReadIndex path in two configurations of the same removal: a reduced configuration with a single voter (node 2) and a reduced configuration with two voters (nodes 2 and 3), in both cases after the remaining voters elected a leader and committed a entry the removed leader never receives.
assumptions: Two scenarios in one process: voters {1,2} where the removal leaves {2}, and voters {1,2,3} where the removal leaves {2,3}; ReadOnlySafe and default Config (StepDownOnRemoval false, CheckQuorum false, PreVote false).

In each scenario node 1 is elected leader, the application proposes and applies the committed removal of node 1 on every node, the remaining voters then elect node 2 and commit one entry, and only then is the ReadIndex request delivered to node 1.
Nothing from the current configuration carries a higher term back to node 1, so the removed leader stays at its old term while the observations are taken.
excluded: Lease-based reads (ReadOnlyLeaseBased).
Check-quorum and pre-vote configurations, which give the removed leader another way to learn that it is stale.
Snapshot transfer and asynchronous storage writes.

experiment.prefix: Scenario A (single-voter remainder): elect node 1 in {1,2}, apply the committed removal of node 1, elect node 2 in {2} and commit one proposal, deliver MsgReadIndex to node 1, then deliver the same request to node 2, then run three heartbeat intervals on node 1 and deliver a second MsgReadIndex to node 1. Scenario B (two-voter remainder): elect node 1 in {1,2,3}, apply the committed removal of node 1 on all three nodes, elect node 2 in {2,3} and commit one proposal, deliver MsgReadIndex to node 1, then run three heartbeat intervals on node 1 and observe whether any answer is produced.
experiment.requirement: A ReadIndex answer must let the application serve a linearizable read (raft.go:233-244 and README.md:27-32 state that ReadOnlySafe achieves linearizability by communicating with the quorum, and node.go:218-224 states that once the application advances past the returned read index, linearizable reads issued before the request can be processed safely). The tracker's own comment for IsSingleton says the single voting member is the leader, so answering locally without any check is only sound when that member is the local node.
experiment.responsibility: raft (target): the singleton shortcut in the ReadIndex path decides the answer for the whole configuration, and the library already refuses proposals from a leader that is not in its own configuration.

comparisons.description: Scenario A premise: the node whose removal the application applied is still leading a configuration whose single voter is another node.
Scenario A premise: the actual leader of the reduced configuration has committed an entry the removed leader's commit index does not cover.
Scenario A witness: the removed leader answered the read with an index below the commit index of the actual leader, sending no message at all.
Scenario A control: the same request answered by the actual leader returns an index that covers its commit index.
Scenario A persistence: after three heartbeat intervals without replies the removed leader repeats the same stale index.
Scenario B premise: the same removal leaves a configuration with two voters, so the singleton shortcut cannot apply to the removed leader (config voters=(2 3)).
Scenario B premise: the new leader of {2,3} has committed an entry the removed leader's commit index does not cover.

Scenario B control outcome: the same read delivered to the removed leader produces no answer at all, and the leader instead enters the readOnly round (heartbeats_emitted 2 with a read context) - the stale immediate answer is specific to the singleton configuration.

Scenario B second symptom: the accepted read stays in readOnly.unconfirmed_reads because the current configuration never acknowledges the removed leader's old-term heartbeats, so no repair exists for it inside raft.
Scenario B persistence: three further heartbeat intervals still produce no answer and no reply from the current configuration.

The comparison set keeps the earlier scenario and adds the control's observations, so the stale immediate answer can be distinguished from the alternative explanation that the removed leader simply keeps working as a leader for reads.

scope.description: Observe the whole interval of one postponed ReadIndex request on a real 4-node group: the leader postpones it, the application then applies an already-committed configuration change whose resulting configuration commits the leader's first entry of the term, the acknowledgement of the previous configuration arrives late, a heartbeat round runs, and finally an unrelated proposal is committed.
assumptions: Four voters {1,2,3,4} bootstrapped from a ConfState-only snapshot, with log entries 1..9 ordinary and entry 10 the configuration change, HardState{Term:1, Commit:10}, applied index 10 (the application has reported applied progress but has not yet called ApplyConfChange for entry 10, which node.go:166-187 permits).

Transport preserves raft's per-message semantics (each message is Stepped by its target and resulting messages are delivered in order); voters are reachable for votes; voter 4 is unreachable and voter 3's append acknowledgements are delayed, which is the message-loss/delay part of the fault model.
The applied change is taken from the log entry at index 10 exactly as an application does when it applies CommittedEntries.
excluded: Pre-vote, check-quorum and lease-based reads (all disabled by the test configuration stub).
Snapshot-based recovery and asynchronous storage writes.

basis.prefix: For each case: build four nodes whose storage is bootstrapped with the case ConfState (voters {1,2,3,4}, or the joint configuration voters {1,2,3} + voters_outgoing {1,2,3,4}), append ten term-1 entries with entry 10 the case configuration change, persist HardState{Term:1,Commit:10} and set Applied=10; then elect node 1 with a real MsgHup/MsgVote/MsgVoteResp round (voter 4 unreachable, voter 3's MsgAppResp delayed), deliver the client's MsgReadIndex, apply the committed change at index 10 via applyConfChange, deliver the delayed acknowledgement, run one heartbeat round (tick), and finally propose one unrelated entry.
basis.requirement: A ReadIndex request that a leader accepts by postponing (raft.go:1363-1368) must be answered once the leader has committed an entry of its term, whichever path performs that commit (raft.go:1550-1554 for the MsgAppResp path, raft.go:2013-2028 for the switchToConfig path), because the helper that discharges the duty is guarded only by committedEntryInCurrentTerm() (raft.go:2127-2145) and the caller's comment states the release is due once the committed index has progressed for the term.
basis.responsibility: raft (target): the leader is the producer of the answer for a request it accepted, and switchToConfig is part of raft, not of the application.

comparisons.description: Precondition observation: the leader postponed the received request because no entry of its term was committed (committed_entry_term 1, leader_term 2).

Witness: applying the committed removal of voter 4 performed the leader's first commit of term 2 (committed 10 -> 11, committed_entry_term 2 == leader_term), so the postponed request is due to be answered, but it is still pending and no ReadState was produced.
Variant of the same cause: applying the committed zero change left the joint configuration, so the incoming half committed the leader's first term-2 entry, yet the postponed request is still pending.

No repair from the periodic round: two heartbeats are sent with an empty read context (heartbeat_ctx_len 0), the delayed acknowledgement of the previous configuration is already in place (match_3 11), and no ReadState is produced.

Control: an unrelated proposal committed by the new configuration releases the postponed request (released_request_ctx A), so the release mechanism works and is reached only through the MsgAppResp commit path.
Control for the joint variant: the postponed request is only released once the unrelated proposal is committed.

scope.description: Observe what raft answers for a ReadIndex request that arrives at a node which the application removed from its configuration while it was leading (StepDownOnRemoval false), after the remaining voter has become leader of the reduced single-voter configuration and committed an entry the removed leader never receives.
assumptions: Two voters {1,2} in one process, ReadOnlySafe, default Config (StepDownOnRemoval false, CheckQuorum false, PreVote false).

Snapshot transfer and asynchronous storage writes.

comparisons.description: The node whose removal the application applied is still leading, with a configuration whose single voter is another node (singleton true, is_voter false).
The actual leader of the reduced configuration has committed an entry that the removed leader's commit index does not cover (committed 4 vs 2).

Witness: the removed leader answered the ReadIndex request with index 2, below the commit index 4 the actual leader already had, without sending any message (heartbeats_emitted 0, messages_emitted empty, pending_reads 0).

result.summary: Bound the removed-leader ReadIndex finding with a same-cause control and requested one execution. Change this turn: the harness assurance_singleton_test.go now also runs the identical two-voter removal inside a three-voter cluster, so the reduced configuration keeps two voters and the singleton shortcut cannot apply to the removed leader, and the comparison set keeps the earlier single-voter scenario (5 comparisons) while adding 5 for the control. The control was verified natively: after the removal node 1 is still StateLeader with config voters=(2 3), is_voter false and singleton false while the new leader of {2,3} has committed index 4 against the removed leader's 2; the same read then produces no answer at all (read_states 0, read_answered false) and instead enters the readOnly round (2 heartbeats carrying a read context, unconfirmed_reads 1), and three further heartbeat intervals with no reply leave it unanswered with unconfirmed_reads still 1 - so the stale immediate answer is specific to the single-voter remainder, and the same missing membership check has a second symptom, an accepted read that nothing inside raft can confirm. No interpretation was added this turn, so the question's recorded account is unchanged until this receipt exists; the expected outcome is that the control comparisons hold and the unconfirmed-read comparisons are violated.

Node 2 campaigns and commits one entry; no message from the current configuration reaches node 1 (its heartbeats at the old term are ignored by node 2 because CheckQuorum and PreVote are disabled).
excluded: Lease-based reads (ReadOnlyLeaseBased).
Check-quorum and pre-vote configurations, which give a leader another way to learn that it is stale.
Snapshot transfer and asynchronous storage writes.

after.description: Observe the removed-leader ReadIndex path in two configurations of the same removal: a reduced configuration with a single voter (node 2) and a reduced configuration with two voters (nodes 2 and 3), in both cases after the remaining voters elected a leader and committed a entry the removed leader never receives.
assumptions: Two scenarios in one process: voters {1,2} where the removal leaves {2}, and voters {1,2,3} where the removal leaves {2,3}; ReadOnlySafe and default Config (StepDownOnRemoval false, CheckQuorum false, PreVote false).

In each scenario node 1 is elected leader, the application proposes and applies the committed removal of node 1 on every node, the remaining voters then elect node 2 and commit one entry, and only then is the ReadIndex request delivered to node 1.
Nothing from the current configuration carries a higher term back to node 1, so the removed leader stays at its old term while the observations are taken.
excluded: Lease-based reads (ReadOnlyLeaseBased).
Check-quorum and pre-vote configurations, which give the removed leader another way to learn that it is stale.
Snapshot transfer and asynchronous storage writes.

prefix.before: Elect node 1 leader of {1,2} with a real MsgHup/MsgVote round, let the application apply the committed empty entry, propose and apply the removal of node 1 on both nodes, then elect node 2 in the reduced configuration {2} and commit one proposal on it; then issue MsgReadIndex to node 1, then the same request to node 2, then three heartbeat intervals on node 1 and a second MsgReadIndex to node 1.
prefix.after: Scenario A (single-voter remainder): elect node 1 in {1,2}, apply the committed removal of node 1, elect node 2 in {2} and commit one proposal, deliver MsgReadIndex to node 1, then deliver the same request to node 2, then run three heartbeat intervals on node 1 and deliver a second MsgReadIndex to node 1. Scenario B (two-voter remainder): elect node 1 in {1,2,3}, apply the committed removal of node 1 on all three nodes, elect node 2 in {2,3} and commit one proposal, deliver MsgReadIndex to node 1, then run three heartbeat intervals on node 1 and observe whether any answer is produced.

before.description: The node whose removal the application applied is still leading, with a configuration whose single voter is another node (singleton true, is_voter false).
The actual leader of the reduced configuration has committed an entry that the removed leader's commit index does not cover (committed 4 vs 2).

Witness: the removed leader answered the ReadIndex request with index 2, below the commit index 4 the actual leader already had, without sending any message (heartbeats_emitted 0, messages_emitted empty, pending_reads 0).

Control: the same request answered by the node that is the actual leader of the configuration returns an index that covers its commit index, so the local singleton answer is only unsafe on the node that is no longer the voter.

No repair from the periodic path: after three heartbeat intervals and no replies from the current configuration, the removed leader is still leading at its old term and still answers with the same stale index.

after.description: Scenario A premise: the node whose removal the application applied is still leading a configuration whose single voter is another node.
Scenario A premise: the actual leader of the reduced configuration has committed an entry the removed leader's commit index does not cover.
Scenario A witness: the removed leader answered the read with an index below the commit index of the actual leader, sending no message at all.
Scenario A control: the same request answered by the actual leader returns an index that covers its commit index.
Scenario A persistence: after three heartbeat intervals without replies the removed leader repeats the same stale index.
Scenario B premise: the same removal leaves a configuration with two voters, so the singleton shortcut cannot apply to the removed leader (config voters=(2 3)).
Scenario B premise: the new leader of {2,3} has committed an entry the removed leader's commit index does not cover.

Scenario B control outcome: the same read delivered to the removed leader produces no answer at all, and the leader instead enters the readOnly round (heartbeats_emitted 2 with a read context) - the stale immediate answer is specific to the singleton configuration.

Scenario B second symptom: the accepted read stays in readOnly.unconfirmed_reads because the current configuration never acknowledges the removed leader's old-term heartbeats, so no repair exists for it inside raft.
Scenario B persistence: three further heartbeat intervals still produce no answer and no reply from the current configuration.

experiments.revision_reason: The harness now also contains the control scenario for the same cause: the identical two-voter removal but with a three-voter cluster, so the reduced configuration has two voters and the singleton shortcut does not apply to the removed leader. The comparison set keeps the earlier scenario and adds the control's observations, so the stale immediate answer can be distinguished from the alternative explanation that the removed leader simply keeps working as a leader for reads.
